problem: Visual navigation policies are limited by small curated datasets (dozens of hours). Large passive data (crowd-sourced teleop with noisy actions, action-free web video) is hard to use, since raw/filtered actions, SLAM, VPT and GCP relabeling all degrade under noise and distribution shift.
motivation: Generalizable end-to-end navigation needs diverse data, but curated collection is costly. Crowd-sourced robot data (FrodoBots-2K, 2000 h) and YouTube video offer coverage, but their actions are unusable. A short-horizon model-based expert can produce cleaner actions by connecting nearby states through a forward model rather than imitating noisy labels.
key_idea: Train a short-horizon relabeling policy with a differentiable forward-model objective (model-based learning) on noisy data, use it to relabel actions on passive datasets, and distill them into a long-horizon GPS/goal-pose conditioned policy (LogoNav).
insight: Because the relabeler optimizes actions through a forward model (reach the goal, avoid collisions, smoothness) instead of imitating noisy actions, it can exploit the full noisy dataset. In Table 'MBRA vs GCP', GCP degrades with more FrodoBots data (GS 0.375 at 100%; best at 1%), while MBRA reaches GS 1.000 with 40-100% of the data. Visual SLAM fails on fisheye/crowded videos (GS 0.125), whereas MBRA-labeled YouTube data gives 0.875.
method: Preprocessing: bidirectional EKF fuses raw actions, wheel speed, GPS and compass to smooth FrodoBots-2K poses; long pauses are filtered, leaving ~700 h.

MBRA short-horizon relabeler π^s: takes the current and goal images (goal up to 20 steps ahead) and outputs N=8 velocity actions at 3 Hz. It is trained with a model-based loss J_mbl=Σ(s_ref−s_i)² over rollouts of a differentiable unicycle model that also counts collision points from estimated depth point clouds and penalizes action differences.
System-delay handling: the network takes delay L and previous actions as input (EfficientNet-B0 encoders + Transformer/MLP) to avoid overshooting.
Relabeling: the frozen π^s relabels the FrodoBots-2K trajectories (and action-free YouTube videos, 100 h) with cleaned 8-step pose trajectories using far goals.

LogoNav long-horizon policy π^l: conditioned on a 2D relative goal pose (up to ~100 goal steps, ~33 s), distilled by imitation J_il on MBRA labels, co-trained with the clean GNM data mixture; PD controller at inference, and the L-th output step is used to handle delay.
Deployment: GPS/tracking-camera subgoals every ~80 m (goal reached within 5 m); a topological graph is used for the short-horizon image-goal policy.

setting.backbone: EfficientNet-B0 + Transformer (MBRA relabeler); MLP goal-pose encoder + Transformer (LogoNav), trained from scratch
setting.training_data: GNM curated datasets (RECON, GO Stanford, CoryHall, TartanDrive, HuRoN, Seattle, SCAND) + FrodoBots-2K (2000 h, ~700 h after filtering) relabeled by MBRA; optionally 100 h YouTube walking-tour video (LeLaN list)
setting.observation: monocular RGB (current + goal image, history) for the relabeler; current RGB + 2D goal pose for LogoNav
setting.action_space: 8-step waypoint trajectory at 3 Hz (integrated linear/angular velocity), tracked with a PD controller
setting.privileged: GPS / tracking-camera (T265) for robot position and goals at test time; topological image graph for the image-goal policy

numbers_note: All results are the authors' own real-world metrics (goal success GS, coverage COV/SC), not standard simulator benchmarks. Sample sizes are small (e.g. 21 or 24 trials).
results: LogoNav with MBRA gets GS 0.857 / COV 0.924 on GPS-goal navigation, versus 0.619 / 0.757 for the best baseline (BC with GCP relabeling) and 0.333 for NoMaD. It navigates 300+ m and transfers to a quadruped and an indoor robot. In six countries, MBRA short-horizon reaches GS 0.958 versus 0.792 for GCP with 1% data.
limitations: The model-based approach depends on an accurate robot/forward model and can generate unreasonable actions. It may be hard to extend to tasks like manipulation.
The forward model lacks rich 3D geometry, semantics and dynamic pedestrian behavior, and human preferences are only implicitly inherited.
Evaluations are small-scale real-world trials, with no standard benchmarks.
